# Devices, Totems and companion commands

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 132 targeted checks and 1,200 reconfiguration states.** This is the lifecycle and shared-command overlay for 74 supplied Tinker/Shaman passages and three frozen shared paragraphs. It does not certify all effects on those cards, all companions, or the whole game.

The [source register](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves all exact procedures and hashes. The [source check](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) and [behavior check](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) cover this bounded package. The other 157 passages in the wider companion inventory are still open. Original sources and the frozen class guide remain unchanged.

The original names, costs, targets, rolls, damage, class gates and frequencies control. A label such as “device,” “deployed” or “support command” below is a classification, not an added ability. **NEW** marks an integration decision explicitly discussed with the notebook.

## At the table

Keep one card/token for each active device, Totem or companion. Record its current HP, expiry, occupied capacity, spent ammunition/uses and protected disablement. A persistent Anacite Drone also retains an ownership identity across reconstruction.

When a device reaches 0 HP, release its active slot and record what destroyed it. A destroyed Drone remains a recoverable machine. Standard summoned companions disappear. Totems stop their aura immediately. Expiry, dismissal, replacement and loss of concentration end effects without producing destruction rewards.

Repair is not reconstruction. Field Repair and Repair Pulse cannot bring a destroyed machine back. Snap Rebuild and the Drone's ten-minute repair can do so under their exact costs, ranges and limits. Snap must still fit the original slot footprint and beat the original expiry.

All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and one damaging companion action per numbered round. Separate tokens, multiclass companions, an extra Action or an extra turn do not reset those limits.

## Lifecycle and persistent state

Primary state is deployed, retracted, destroyed, expired, ended or replaced. Protected disablement is a separate flag. A disabled Drone can be retracted or destroyed; neither action clears the flag. An active entity functions only while deployed, before its expiry, above 0 HP if it has HP, available in its owner's configuration, and not disabled.

**NEW:** administrative ending releases capacity without destruction, refunds or salvage. Earlier destruction debris can remain after the original timer, but cannot be Snap Rebuilt at or after that timer. Inert remnants do not acquire collision, cover, terrain or repair rights without a source.

The Drone has an asset identity for ownership and configuration and an instance identity for the current physical incarnation. Ordinary repair, retraction, redeployment, Snap and Reconfiguration preserve that instance. A genuinely new paid deployment or explicit long-rest Drone rebuild uses a new instance.

Protected disablement belongs to the persistent Drone asset. A long-rest rebuild can therefore produce a full-HP Drone that remains disabled. The printed automatic clearance is a completed **short rest**; a long rest is not silently substituted for that marker.

## Commands, Reactions and damage allowances

| Event | Shared BA command | Shared damaging action | Other payment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Attack command | Spent | Spent | Printed costs |
| Support-only command | Spent | Available | Printed costs |
| Gadget Sync shot | Unchanged | Spent | Trigger and 1 RP |
| Decoy Dummy destruction damage | Unchanged | Spent if available | Automatic engine trigger |
| Default follow/move/Dodge | Unchanged | Unchanged | No attack granted |
| Emergency Protocols, Protective Programming, Magnetic Wall | Unchanged | Unchanged | Owner's printed Reaction |
| Volatile Components / Cinderflame destruction burst | Unchanged | Unchanged | Their own predicates and limits |

Gadget Sync after support may use the still-unspent damaging allowance. Gadget Sync first leaves a later BA support command available. Neither sequence grants a second damaging activation. Rocket Tower's two-target shot is one activation; Advanced Turret Bay does not command both turrets together.

**NEW scope clarification:** engine[6]'s damaging-trigger limit applies to its deployable profiles, including Decoy. It does not impose that limit on separately printed Volatile Components or Cinderflame. A suppressed Decoy trigger grants no damage and is not banked. An off-turn Decoy trigger still uses the current numbered-round allowance. Tinker BA commands also require their narrower regular-turn eligibility. Other timing/trigger legality is checked by the caller.

Nano Aegis uses a support command for each printed BA+1RP output; it cannot attack with that command. Its reviewed maximum of three outputs remains. Duration extensions do not restore ammo, uses or healing pulses.

## Durability and immunities

| Profile | Maximum / initial HP | AC | Stat timing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anacite Drone | max(1, 5 + actual INT modifier + Tinker level) | 13 + actual INT modifier | Current actual owner values |
| Ordinary HP-bearing deployable | 2 × Tinker level | 12 + PB | NEW creation snapshot |
| Deployable Expertise on eligible object | Add M maximum/initial HP | Add 1 | Creation; excludes Drones |
| Totem, including Echo | 2 × Shaman level | 12 + PB | NEW placement snapshot |
| Named standard elemental | 2L; Harmony makes 3L | 12 + floor(PB/2) | Creation |
| Elemental Chorus package | 4L; Harmony makes 5L total | 12 + PB | Creation |
| Salvage / Reaper Scrapling | L | 12 | Creation |
| Restoration Field | No HP-bearing anchor | None | Slot effect |

A legitimate temporary actual INT change updates Drone AC, maximum HP and its current PB+INT attack bonus. Increased maximum supplies capacity without healing. Decreased maximum clamps current HP without damage or destruction. Finite created profiles keep their creation statistics.

Harmony adds HP at creation and one source turn of duration, capped at four. It does not heal an existing summon. Chorus is one shared package represented by four spirits. Echo's 10-foot radius and half aura numbers do not halve its durability.

Machines/Totem objects have no organic Wounds, Stable state or death saves. Legal temporary HP is a separate buffer. The Drone's printed poison/psychic and Charmed immunities do not imply every condition immunity. Totems have their own printed poison/psychic and condition immunities. “Vulnerable to ordinary weapon and other damage” means susceptible in this source wording, not an invented numerical doubling.

The reference's damage method receives an amount after all legally applicable defenses. Condition eligibility, object immunities, attack rolls, saves and exact riders remain caller work. A Shaman elemental is a creature companion, not automatically a machine.

Scraplings are temporary companions with their printed stats and shared command rules. Neither supplied Scrapling source establishes generic machine/device targeting. Salvage's slot cost does not grant that category. They disappear at zero HP and do not thereby gain Field Repair, Repair Pulse, protected-disable routing, Recycling, Volatile Components, Snap or other device-only permissions.

## Repair, reconstruction and disabling

| Procedure | Eligible target and change | Payment / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field Repair | Touched damaged machine with positive HP; or protected-disabled positive-HP machine, even at full HP. An available carried/retracted Drone qualifies. Restores rolled S d8+M up to max and clears protected disablement | Action, 1 RP, printed Recharge 2 |
| Repair Pulse | Up to three functional friendly devices; restores floor(maxHP/2), applies printed +1 AC until next source start. Does not clear protected disablement | Action, 3 RP, 1/short rest |
| Drone ten-minute reconstruction | Destroyed owned Drone with available original material; restores max(1, floor(maxHP/2)); preserves protected disablement | 10 minutes, 1 RP, 1/short rest |
| Snap Rebuild | Destroyed device/Drone, legal material, original free compatible slot footprint and remaining duration; restores max(1, floor(maxHP/2)); preserves disablement | BA, 2 RP, 1/encounter |
| Disable-clear tools procedure | Clears only protected-disable flag, including on a destroyed persistent machine; restores no HP | Separate 10 minutes, 1 RP, tinker's tools |
| Completed short rest | Clears protected disablement only | Actual completed short-rest marker |
| Long-rest Drone rebuild | Full HP, fresh physical instance for owned asset, even after old material consumed; preserves uncleared asset disablement | Actual source-authorized completed long rest |

**NEW machine viability arithmetic:** explicit half-maximum reconstruction has minimum 1 HP. Repair Pulse on a functional max-1-HP machine still restores floor(1/2) = 0.

The two ten-minute procedures are distinct rights. Reconstructing a disabled, destroyed Drone does not also buy disable clearance. Reconstruction is not a generic cleanse and does not reset ammunition, modules, spent uses, Overdrive history or unexpired legal effects. Normally damage has already consumed temp HP before destruction; this package adds no destroyed-machine temp-HP grant.

Routing Dissonance is the engine[7] BA, once/short rest, up to two current Dissonance into an active device within 30 feet. It creates no RP, does not reset Refrain, and blocks movement, attacks, auras and triggers while the device's timer continues.

## Capacity, placement and dependent Totems

Deployable slots are zero before the engine's class gate, one at Tinker 6, two at 13 and three at 17. Advanced Turret Bay uses two available slots for 4 RP, or its one-slot/2-RP fallback; zero free slots is illegal. Drones use separate persistent ownership capacity, not deployable slots.

At Tinker 13, choose exactly two basic Drones with exactly one module each or exactly one Drone with exactly two distinct modules during the printed configuration procedure. No more than two. Earlier module acquisition remains governed by its own class gates. **NEW:** withdrawing the excess Drone into an unavailable/retracted configuration causes no destruction or salvage.

Totem capacity is one, then two at Shaman 13. **NEW generalization:** an ordinary new Totem placed at capacity replaces a chosen active Totem, including at capacity one. Echo needs a separate free capacity; creating Echo alone never evicts another Totem.

**NEW dependent Echo rule:** ending, replacing, destroying or expiring the parent ends its Echo and releases both capacities. That Echo ending is administrative, not its own destruction. Ending only Echo leaves the parent. Echo shares the parent's remaining duration, concentration and upkeep.

Preflight ownership, source use, space/range, action, resources and capacity before payment or ending anything. Determine all dependent releases first. A valid parent replacement can free room for the new parent plus a separately paid Echo. If Echo cannot fit, its optional creation is unavailable; the caller can submit an ordinary parent-only placement instead. Failure of a submitted combined transaction changes nothing.

All active Totems share their concentration burden. Losing it ends their effects and dependent Echoes without destruction rewards. Totem movement follows its printed BA, 15-foot move through an open route within the printed range; it retains expiry, concentration, recipient ledgers and pulse schedule. Movement grants no entry heal.

## Destruction, debris and source-specific opportunities

Record the instance, original hostile cause, actual enemy hit versus transferred damage, deliberate sacrifice, whether the object itself is a copy, friendly damage, secondary explosion and inherited branch flags at destruction. Separately record whether incoming damage was copied. A real device destroyed by copied damage still has ordinary destruction consequences; only that damage's actual restriction flags suppress them. “Copied object” exclusions do not mean “any object damaged by a copy.”

**NEW anti-loop integration:** the first actual destruction of an instance establishes its only object-linked opportunity and material set. Nonqualifying and declined opportunities are closed for that instance. Snap does not create another set. A second physical destruction still ends the rebuilt device but cannot supply another harvest, Volatile opportunity or material record.

Recycling, Salvage, Reaper and Snap share the usable original material. The first successful consumer spends it. Volatile does not consume material. A source-qualified Volatile can therefore precede one legal material consumer. Declining Volatile on Device A does not spend the owner's round allowance for Device B.

| Source | Important predicate |
| --- | --- |
| Efficient Recycling | Your destroyed non-copy device; not deliberate sacrifice; debris within reach, after combat for one minute, 1/short rest. Refund at most min(1 RP, actual deployment RP). Enemy cause is **not required**. |
| Scrap Salvage | Enemy-destroyed qualifying material; Action+1 RP, 1/encounter; one slot-using Scrapling at printed location |
| Scrap Reaper | Qualifying destroyed enemy-hit device/material within 30 feet; Reaction+2 RP, 1/short rest; printed short-lived Scrapling uses **no deployable slot** |
| Volatile Components | First enemy-caused device destruction; excludes deliberate sacrifice, copy, friendly damage and secondary explosion; enemy within 5 feet; once per owner/round |
| Snap | Original destroyed instance/material, original footprint free and original expiry not reached |

Scraplings cannot spawn their own replacement. Reaper still uses the later BA command and damaging-action budget for its detonation. Its absent slot cost is not inferred from the separate Salvage card. Reaper also carries its source's broader no-own-destruction-chain property; a later type ruling must not silently remove that protection.

Inherited noResourceGeneration blocks Recycling refunds. It does not automatically prohibit all non-resource transformations. Inherited noRetaliation blocks a destruction explosion such as Volatile. Inherited noDeathTriggers blocks Volatile, Cinder's destruction burst and Reaper's destruction-triggered Reaction. It does not automatically prohibit the later Action-based Scrap Salvage or ordinary Recycling. Source-specific exclusions still apply to each consumer.

Cinderflame's qualifying destruction event is captured before its standard-companion disappearance. Its printed burst may then resolve, with the printed three-enemy cap, save, damage and no further death/resource triggers. Dismissal, expiry and concentration ending are not destruction.

Volatile Injection spends M **normal** device HP and requires current HP strictly greater than M. Temp HP cannot pay it. It is not damage or a qualifying destruction event. Deliberate sacrifice sources retain their express no-proc/salvage/copy/refund exclusions.

## Magnetic Wall and existing damage sharing

**NEW source binding and timing integration:** when the printed ranged weapon hit, ally distance and wall-line predicates hold, the owner's Reaction transfers exactly min(remaining defended damage, S+M) to the functional Wall after the ally's ordinary defenses/prevention and before temp HP.

The transfer retains damage type. The Wall branch carries noSecondMitigation and noRetransfer. It receives no second AC roll, critical, attack-hit rider or second mitigation pass. Legal Wall temp HP then normal HP absorb it; reaching zero destroys it and releases its slot.

Enemy damage intercepted this way remains enemy-caused. Choosing the Reaction is not deliberate sacrifice. A Wall destroyed this way may qualify Volatile and a source-qualified material consumer. Transferred damage is not itself an attack hit on the Wall; enemy-hit-only Reaper qualification remains distinct.

Emergency Protocols retains its existing additional noRetaliation flag. Enemy attribution and ordinary debris survive, but destroying the Drone cannot bypass that flag to trigger Volatile. This new Magnetic Wall binding supplements the earlier 39-source redirection package; it was not part of that package's original count.

## Reconfiguration and implementation boundaries

Reconfiguration requires a functional deployed device and a known eligible nonhealing destination. **NEW arithmetic:** newHP = max(1, floor(oldHP × newMaxHP / oldMaxHP)), capped at new max. Preserve instance, slot footprint, expiry, ammunition, spent uses, destruction history and effect clocks. This conversion is neither damage nor healing.

Pending modifiers only apply when their own predicate remains true. Overcharge grants no free command; a profile unable to use it does not refund it or reset its deadline. Exact source access, profile legality and pending-modifier application remain caller responsibilities.

Restoration Field is a slot-using concentration effect with its already-reviewed healing scheduler. Its source supplies no HP, AC or physical anchor. It cannot be attacked as a fabricated machine, repaired, Snap Rebuilt, Remote Detonated, used for Volatile Injection/salvage or targeted by protected Dissonance routing merely because it consumes a slot.

The implementation stores authoritative owner/instance/material identifiers, original ClockMarkers, canonical command ledgers, atomic RP/action payments and explicit source-scoped use keys. The caller must provide the same real owner wallet and ledger across abilities, unique use-scope keys tied to the real rest/encounter calendar, legal source actions and costs, actual targets/geometry, source profiles and class gates. It must also propagate these life states to the pulse/concentration engine.

All timed device effects supplied here expire during a completed long rest, explaining the fresh Drone instance's empty timed-effect list and zero tempHP. This is not a generic reconstruction cleanse: a future permanent or long-rest-surviving source effect must retain its own clock and rules.

This reference does not create a complete runtime transaction manager, movement/collision system, all damage riders, every condition interaction, all 157 remaining companion candidates or a video game. It supplies the same decisions in tabletop prose and a precise checked model for later implementation.

## Discussion evidence

Saved in docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game:

# Forms and temporary HP

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED — selected form and temporary-HP interfaces.** This overlay covers 175 exact source roles, five support passages, 26 Druid form profiles and selected common interfaces. GPT approved the corrected reference and its clock-initialization addendum; 165 contract checks and 1,053 shield/damage scenarios pass. It does not close full class cards, feats, ancestry, ordinary spell catalogs, equipment or the whole game. Original cards and historical text remain unchanged in the [source register](FORM_TEMP_HP_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md). Use the [Druid form quick reference](DRUID_FORM_QUICK_REFERENCE.md) for the compact form and special-cost tables.

## One active shield

Temporary HP is a single active grant with its own identity, source, owner, recipient, remaining points, endpoint and explicitly attached permissions. A larger new offer replaces it; a smaller or equal offer is discarded. Equal values preserve the existing grant and its deadline. Discarded shields do not remain underneath. A rejected offer cannot lend its duration or linked rider to the winner. A zero offer creates no grant.

Pay the legal source's printed costs before comparing shields. Costs are not refunded because the new shield loses. Druid Buffer Reserve pays the entire offered amount, not just the increase over an existing shield. Preflight actual source access, targets, geometry, actions, components and resources before paying anything; illegal activations spend nothing.

Unless the source states a different shield lifetime, a grant ends at the recipient's next completed long rest. “Until lost” or “until lost or replaced” only restates depletion; it does not exempt a grant from that default. Explicit fixed deadlines and source dependencies take precedence, even when they outlast a long rest. An ongoing ability's general duration does not automatically shorten an instantaneous shield that it generates.

Temporary HP absorbs post-defense damage before normal HP. It is not healing: it cannot stabilize, revive, wake an Unconscious creature, remove Wounds, reset death counters or pay direct/sacrificial HP costs. A living creature at0 can receive it without gaining any of those benefits. A dead body is not a valid holder. A prohibition on HP healing does not implicitly prohibit a separately legal shield.

## Exact endpoints and riders

Use actual owner/recipient regular-turn markers, absolute deadlines and encounter identities, not extra-turn or copied clocks. Source-specific rules remain in the exact card; this table resolves the important ambiguities.

| Source | Shield endpoint / linked boundary |
|---|---|
| Crimson Bloodshield | End of its three owner turns. Its one Reaction is attached only to its accepted grant; depletion/replacement/expiry removes permission. |
| Bloodbond; Lingering Malice | Each trigger/pulse makes a default long-rest grant; ending concentration does not erase it. |
| Nature's Blessing; Dread Shelter; Nano-Aegis command | Start/cast/command shield uses default long-rest lifetime; Speed, DR and support mode keep their separate clocks. |
| Protective Programming | Offer before the triggering hit. Resolve that hit, then remove any remainder of this particular grant. A stronger unrelated shield that won comparison is unaffected. |
| Monk Support; Warder Arrow and capstone | Default long-rest grants. Permanent availability or an instantaneous attack is not a permanent shield. |
| Harmonized Core; Arcane Leech; Primordial Surge; King's Smite; Noble Bearing | Default long-rest lifetime, including the sources that merely say “until lost.” |
| Linked Ward | After the actual triggering packet, default long-rest grant. |
| Final Stand | After actual triggering packet; shield and triggered resistance end at the ally's next regular end. The redirection itself ends at the Paladin's next regular start. **New grammatical integration.** |
| Unbroken Covenant | Until the Lock ends; this clause is explicit in preserved source provenance. |
| Last King's Gift | After damage, until encounter end. Its existing death-prevention gate remains separate. |
| Soldier Rally Point | Shield until encounter end; next-save bonus only until Soldier's next regular start. |
| Soldier Rallying Cry | Encounter end. |
| Dragoon Bastion Descent | Shield until Dragoon's next regular start; resistance until used or that start; cleanse instantaneous. **New grammatical integration.** |
| Bear / Earth Warden | Bound to that form instance; no refill at renewal. |
| Mooncursed ally Howl | Independent default long-rest grants, surviving Druid reversion. **New bridge clarification.** |
| Overflowing Light | Original two-round endpoint; if this exact grant is still active with at least1 point, allow ending one actual Frightened, Poisoned or Staggered condition. Rejection, replacement, depletion or holder/dependency removal gives no cleanse. Mastery raises only the cap10→20. |
| Protective Verse | One-minute shield and a separate one-minute next-qualifying-save rider. The rider can survive shield replacement. |
| Arcane Sanctuary | Each accepted pulse until owner's next regular start or source end, whichever first. Its attack bonus is a separate zone effect. |
| Empowered Link | Half the eligible source numeric benefit, rounded down/minimum1 where applicable; shared benefit duration capped at owner's next regular end. It cannot share resources, Actions, resistance or other excluded effects. |

Other explicit minute, round, turn and encounter endpoints retain their exact source wording. Cleric return shields, Crimson Pact, Mirrorsage Ward profiles, Mage Resonance Shield and Soulbound use their printed one-minute deadlines. Light Binding ends at owner's next regular end. Momentum Shield, Bolstering Presence, Aura Surge, Black Manifestation, Final Command, Mutation Surge and Wizard Abjuration use their printed next regular start. Momentum Barrier lasts one minute. A source with no specified shield endpoint uses the default.

King's Smite and Noble Bearing first resolve their shared internal component: when Noble applies, produce one Noble offer instead of a King's Smite offer. Each is half actual radiant Smite damage, rounded down, capped atS+M. Then compare that one offer with the recipient's existing shield. Their word “replaces” does not override an unrelated equal shield. Transfer-generated shields use the prior redirection package's actual absorbed amount, single-root restrictions and source caps; they appear after the causal packet and cannot retroactively protect it.

Each excess-healing point has one conversion owner. A source that explicitly converts its own excess has priority over external generic converters. Channel Life's packet forbids excess-to-temp-HP conversion by any provider; independent fixed shields still resolve normally. These are the existing healing interfaces, not a second excess pool.

## Druid: one body throughout

Keep your own HP, ability scores, saves, proficiency, conditions, personality and body identity. No copied monster statistics, separate beast HP or overflow pool exists. Base forms cannot speak; Arch/Hero forms can. Default size Medium, walking30, ordinary senses and operative character AC; change only the printed form traits. Hawk is Tiny; Bear, Earth Warden and Hero forms may be Large if legal space permits. No form invents hands or hand-based equipment use.

Equipment melds and cannot be used. **New AC bridge:** calculate `formNormalAC` from effects that remain operative in the form. Exclude worn armor's AC calculation, shield AC, effects requiring melded equipment use and unclassified item bonuses. A passive magical numeric item bonus requires the equipment adapter to certify anatomy compatibility. Apply the form's exact formula after that calculation, never adding worn armor again. Equipment returns in its prior state on reversion; shifting never repairs, reloads, restores charges or refreshes it. The full item/anatomy matrix remains unfinished.

Five Base forms unlock at1. Choose Circle at2; the chosen Circle's Arch path begins3, with its level6 feature. Circle Hero forms arrive at their printed10/14 gates. At11 attune at most two of the five Arch forms at a completed long rest. This is form acquisition, not another class promotion. All exact profiles and their complete original effects are in [the26-form register](../../data/playtest/druid_form_profiles.json).

At a completed long rest record:

- Shift uses2/3/4/5/6/7/8 at levels1/4/7/10/13/16/19. The conflicting historical schedule remains preserved.
- Buffer Reserve `2 × Druid level + M`.
- Form Surge Reserve `PB`.

These recorded reserves do not refill just because level, proficiency or form changes. At20 shift-use costs become zero, while Buffer Reserve, Surges and source-specific uses remain finite.

To enter a legal different profile, pay a Bonus Action and one shift use below20. End the previous instance and its dependent effects, create a fresh instance lasting10 minutes, clear Refrain's remembered spell/count, and retain Dissonance. Then resolve entry benefits. Bear offers `min(20, reserve)` and Earth Warden `min(30, reserve)`; deduct the whole offer even if a stronger shield wins. Both forms remain legal with reserve0. Natural attacks do not clear Refrain.

Early reversion costs a Bonus Action and no shift use; it does not clear Refrain. An early attempt to enter the already-current identical profile is rejected unpaid. At the exact natural10-minute endpoint, choosing to renew the same profile costs a shift use below20, with no new Bonus Action. Keep the same instance, local uses and existing effects; extend only the form endpoint. Do not refill its buffer, repeat entry effects, clear Refrain or extend a swarm/smoke effect's independent deadline. Declining renewal ends it normally. A later genuine reentry creates a new instance but cannot replenish shared reserves or per-rest abilities.

Elemental subtypes Air/Earth/Fire/Water and Vermin bat/ground choices are part of the profile identity. Switching subtype is a real new entry. Elemental entry additionally spends one of its two long-rest uses; natural renewal of the same subtype spends no new Elemental use. **New bounded profile completion:** Elemental attacks use lightning/bludgeoning/fire/cold respectively; Earth Warden's ordinary claw is slashing. An existing natural form attack without printed reach uses5 feet. These choices import no monster stat block.

## Attacks, specials and ending a form

One Action makes one printed natural attack, using currentPB+actualWIS and current Druid DC. A named Howl, Slam, Breath, summon, Smoke, Blast or Thunder Step replaces that Action's ordinary attack. Preserve each exact range, dice, save, condition and frequency. Natural/form attacks remain explicit categories; unrelated weapon-only procs are not authorized until the missing global taxonomy is reviewed. Expressly natural/form-qualified features such as Circle Forms and Primal Strike still work.

Local Surge use is keyed by actual form instance plus specific special. Legal commitment spends the opportunity and one Surge before rolls; miss/save/failure provides no refund. Mooncursed's ally and enemy Howls share one opportunity. Broodmother Spawn and critical-negation are separate opportunities, each requiring a Surge. Sky Serpent and Tempest's wet bonuses are attack riders, not extra attacks.

Broodmother's optional spawn exists only inside the entry transaction. A legal chosen spawn spends its Surge; an illegal or declined spawn spends none and does not undo entry. Once entry closes, there is no later spawn window for that instance. The separate critical-negation remains available. # Reputation — Canon Interaction Rules

**Status:** Playable canon

Reputation records how Aethel's institutions respond to the character. It is not a morality score and it is not a hidden multiplier on the laws of magic.

## Scale

Faction standing is stored as `{ [factionId]: score }` on the character save, normally from **−3 (Hated)** through **+3 (Honored)**. Backgrounds and play can set or change starting standing.

## What reputation can change

A faction may change:

- prices, credit, insurance, salvage rights, and expedition sponsorship;
- access to restricted libraries, teachers, rituals, recipes, laboratories, temples, circles, and sanctuaries;
- information quality, contacts, safe houses, legal treatment, hostility, and political support;
- availability of a **named** focus, training feature, consumable, or scene benefit whose rules are written explicitly.

## What reputation does not change automatically

Reputation does **not** silently modify:

- a spell's Resonance Rank;
- base RP cost;
- natural maximum RP;
- Dissonance gained from a cast;
- the Frayed / Discordant / Fractured thresholds;
- a character's moral alignment.

If a guild teaches a cheaper technique or a shrine grants a recovery boon, that is an explicit earned benefit, not proof that the Weave itself favors members of that institution.

## Magic connection

The universal magic rules are in [`RESONANCE_CANON.md`](./RESONANCE_CANON.md). Faction standing can provide **tools for dealing with magic**, but never rewrites the underlying resonance law merely because the character is liked or hated.

## Companion implementation

- `src/data/reputation.js` owns faction definitions and starting standing.
- `character-storage.js` persists the reputation map.
- `resonance-economy.js` retains compatibility helper names for old saves/code, but automatic reputation-to-RP and reputation-to-spell-cost modifiers return **0** under current canon.

This separation is deliberate: institutions matter socially and materially; Resonance/Dissonance remain metaphysical rules.

# Strain — source-qualified playtest reference

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the supplied namespace, penalty and recovery scope.** [GPT's exact disposition](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FINAL_REVIEW.md) confirms this bounded candidate. The two names below refer to independent systems. This candidate preserves the Warrior engine and retains the Gameplay Loop's expedition track as a provisional campaign overlay. It does not promote that older table into the approved Core book.

Use [source bindings](../../data/playtest/strain_bindings.json), [source validation](STRAIN_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [combat timing](COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md), [conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP/Wounds](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). The [first GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FIRST_REVIEW.md) and [counterexample corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_COUNTEREXAMPLE_REVIEW.md) preserve the decisions. The latter corrects an earlier summary that misplaced the expedition attack/save penalties at level3; their source places them at level2.

## Identify the track first

| Mechanical ID | What it represents | Range | Generic recovery |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `warrior.serum-strain` | The Warrior serum/mutation engine, including an explicit Serum Sharing recipient | 0–3 | Beneficial completed1h Short Rest−1; beneficial completed8h Long Rest→0 |
| `expedition.strain` | Campaign attrition, Rest Debt, unsupported Supply, Quickglass crash and ordinary Wound-treatment critical failure | 0–6 | Secure beneficial Long Rest−1 eligible point; Morale Rest−1; qualifying Haven care removes all eligible ordinary points |

Neither is global `core.exhaustion`, Oracle Revelation backlash, Dissonance or historical Resonance Burn. A single cause applies multiple tracks only if its operative source explicitly says so. Serum3 never becomes expedition3, and serum overflow never becomes expedition6. A namespace binding identifies a reference; it does not itself apply any effect.

Inside the supplied Warrior engine/cards, Strain means serum Strain. In the supplied campaign references, Strain means expedition Strain. **Future ambiguous sources remain unbound until reviewed.** The source register records8 Warrior engine references,17 cards,3 campaign sections and12 exact Core paragraphs. Do not classify a new immunity or source by its name alone.

Quickglass's crash adds1 expedition point and retains its independent one-hour DEX-check disadvantage. Ordinary Wound-treatment Critical Failure adds1 expedition point to the **patient**, without inventing another Wound or Exhaustion level. Morale Rest removes expedition Strain only. Serum Tolerance suppresses the profile side effects it names; it does not prevent serum Strain or its penalties.

## Warrior serum Strain

Preserve the source engine: normal Serum Injection/Mutagen Injection and Mutation Surge add1; Serum Cocktail/Mutation Overload add2 unless a printed modifier applies. Cap3. At2, Speed−5. At3, also AC−1 and saves−1; the source's voluntary serum/Cocktail/Overclock/Surge activation lock applies. All card costs, prepared doses, mutation limits and frequencies remain required.

For an activation explicitly illegal if it exceeds the cap, calculate its **final modified gain first**, including applicable Mutation Adaptation and the minimum1 for Cocktail/Overload where applicable. Reject a resulting value above3. Never clip a voluntary overcap cost into legality. A separate activation lock can still prohibit activation even if a gain modifier makes its cost small or zero.

Automatic later gains, such as the actual **Sanguine Surge** profile's ending side effect, clamp at3. They do not retroactively invalidate the original activation, cause overflow death or add expedition points.

**Serum Sharing — NEW integration.** Its willing recipient receives serum Strain even when not a Warrior. At recipient3, the attempted+1 clamps at3; this is not the recipient activating an otherwise locked class ability. The recipient retains all existing penalties and receives only the card's actual diluted effects and side effects. Source-owner Serum Tolerance does not protect the ally. Recipient Strain uses the same beneficial1h/8h recovery; no serum preparation, mutation slots or other Warrior powers are granted.

## Expedition Strain

NEW interpretation: rows are cumulative. Preserve the original placement of effects:

| Level | Additional consequence |
|---:|---|
| 0 | None |
| 1 | −1 initiative and expedition checks |
| 2 | Speed−10; −1 attacks and saving throws |
| 3 | Disadvantage on expedition checks; Dash lock below |
| 4 | Effective maximum HP×3/4 |
| 5 | Core Incapacitated plus the explicit movement restriction below |
| 6 | Deterministic death/collapse endpoint below |

Initiative−1 applies when a roll is made. Changing Strain does not reorder an established encounter. Ordinary advantage/disadvantage does not numerically stack from multiple sources.

Represent each point with `pointId`, `sourceId`, `ordinaryRemovable` and `removalGateMet`. Level is the active count, maximum6. Keep source history and attempted overflow even when no additional point can be stored. A generic recovery can select only points that are ordinary-removable **and** whose gate is met. A specific treatment can override only the source it expressly covers. Clearing a gate updates metadata; it does not silently delete a point.

**Level6 — NEW deterministic interpretation.** On every positive, unprevented expedition gain that would reach **or exceed6**, evaluate that gain's endpoint before clamping stored points at6. Default: ordinary Dead state. Only that gain's explicit reviewed nonlethal source can instead produce `expedition.collapse`. A living collapsed creature already at6 can die from a later ordinary gain; it is not protected by the cap. A prevented/zero gain causes no endpoint. Nonlethal gains or Strain removal never revive a corpse.

Collapse leaves the creature alive, Unconscious, Speed0 and unable to act/travel. It does not set HP0, grant Stable or create death saves by itself. Independently dying0HP creatures still follow their normal saves. Short/Long/Morale Rest cannot reduce expedition points while this level6 collapse persists; qualifying24h Haven care or explicit treatment may. Collapse ends only when the track falls below6. Other Unconscious sources remain independent. If all six points stay blocked, Haven care cannot clear the collapse by assertion.

This recoverable collapse is a **NEW operational replacement** for the source's undefined “permanent collapse” alternative. The original wording remains preserved; it did not itself specify this recovery. Actual resurrection while six expedition points remain is a separate unresolved resurrection interface.

## Independent penalties and maximum HP

Apply flat Speed changes first, floor at0, then applicable multipliers and floor normally. A rule setting Speed0 takes precedence. Serum2's−5 and expedition2's−10 coexist: base30 becomes15, then Exhaustion2's half Speed gives7. Mutation Adaptation's explicit serum Speed exception does not cancel expedition Speed loss.

Expedition2 and serum3 each impose saves−1, totaling−2. The class rule against stacking duplicate bonuses does not merge these independent tracks.

NEW maximum-HP composition: multiply applicable rational factors against the same otherwise-applicable maximum, floor **once**, minimum1. Expedition4×3/4 and Exhaustion4×1/2 produce37 from base100. Clamp currentHP down if necessary; that clamp is not damage and triggers no Wound, death-save failure or damage resource. Removing a modifier raises capacity without healing/resetting death counters. Critical Wounds' healing ceiling then uses `max(1, effectiveMaximumHP−1)`; it is not another maxHP multiplier.

The helper accepts other multipliers only after their compatibility has been established elsewhere. It does not decide whether unrelated gear/ancestry/spell modifiers stack.

## Dash lock — NEW

At expedition3–4, a legal Dash consumes the current opportunity and creates a lock. No other Dash is legal while locked, whether Action, Bonus Action, extra Action or extra turn. A non-Dash Action, round boundary or extra turn does not clear it.

In initiative, lock through the **end of the next future regular turn** of the creature. A Dash during its current turn excludes that current end, using the exact marker-exclusion rule from combat. Thus turn1 Dash blocks another that turn and turn2; turn2's end unlocks turn3. An off-turn Dash locks through the next regular turn's end. Extra turns cannot substitute for that marker.

Outside initiative, unlock at Dash time+6 seconds. Preserve whichever endpoint was recorded across initiative entry/exit/reorder; do not restart or convert it. Falling below expedition3 clears the restriction and stored lock immediately. Returning to3 begins unlocked until a new legal Dash. Expedition5 cannot Dash at all.

The exact review confirms exclusion of the current in-progress turn end. Its earlier “strictly after Dash” shorthand is superseded by these specific marker rules and tests.

## Expedition5 and assistance

Core Incapacitated denies Action/Bonus Action/Reaction and ends concentration. NEW expedition-specific restriction: no voluntary tactical movement in initiative. This does **not** redefine generic Incapacitated or automatically set the creature's actual Speed statistic to0. Forced movement, an external legal teleport and lawful carrying still work.

Outside combat, apply the slow-travel exception by halving the otherwise legal walking/travel pace once after applicable load/Speed/environment rules. Do not repeatedly halve per Watch or invent miles-per-hour values here. Detailed stacking with other travel-pace modifiers remains the travel review's responsibility.

Brief communication is possible if no other condition prevents it. The victim cannot use an Action-time consumable by itself. A legal willing recipient can be fed, given a potion or treated by someone paying the actual required Action/activity, supplies and costs. This creates no free administration or universal restraint/capture rule. Rest and Haven care remain possible when their eligibility requirements are met.

## Recovery and actual elapsed time

Preserve campaign limits: Short Rest1h, at most **two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests**; Long Rest8h, at most **one beneficial Long Rest per24 elapsed hours**. Those limits apply to serum recovery too, including non-Warrior recipients. Exact completion timestamps and IDs prevent replay. Work, travel, short rest, sleep and recreation cannot spend the same active hours twice. Unfinished/interrupted activity provides no completion benefit.

**Rest Debt order.** First complete a qualifying safe8hRestWatch and clear debt it satisfies. Then evaluate beneficial Long Rest eligibility. If eligible, apply its sourced benefits, including serum reset and one eligible expedition point when secure. Persistent food/water/source blocks still prevent expedition reduction. An additional safe RestWatch inside the24h reward cap can discharge debt but cannot restore resources, remove expedition Strain, reset the beneficial-rest clock or reset short-rest counts.

**Secure Long Rest.** Remove one eligible expedition point chosen by the patient, once the rest qualifies and no reduction block remains. This is a separate benefit from serum reset, so one actual qualifying rest may do both. Class-only serum reduction never silently removes expedition points.

**Morale Rest — NEW endpoint.** Four consecutive safe hours of voluntarily chosen recreation, without forced substance use, work, expedition travel or simultaneous sleep/ShortRest. At most one beneficial Morale Rest per24 elapsed hours. Remove one eligible expedition point. It never removes a Wound. A distinct4hMoraleRest plus an eligible8hsecureLongRest can legitimately remove two points; there is no new shared one-point cap.

**Haven care.** One full day means24 consecutive hours under qualifying Haven care/location conditions, with real care, food and water supplied under campaign rules. One active care interval per patient; interrupted care gives no completion benefit and restarting requires a fresh24h window. At completion remove all eligible ordinary expedition points; blocked/special points remain. The care window may contain separate sleep, meals and4h recreation because it is not24h of active practitioner work. Incompatible practitioner activities cannot be double-counted.

The Strain reference does not replace HP/RP/RC rest rewards or settle all supply prices, travel limits or camp security. Those systems retain their source review gates.

## Immunity, suppression and removal

Only explicit source-qualified wording changes a track. Poison immunity, global Exhaustion immunity, serum-profile tolerance and expedition immunity do not automatically cover serum Strain. Exhaustion removal does not clear either track. An unqualified future “immune to Strain” remains unbound.

- “Cannot gain expedition Strain” blocks gains only.
- “Ignore expedition Strain penalties” retains the points; no implied prevention of gain or level6 endpoint.
- “Remove X expedition Strain” actually removes eligible points under that source.

These tracks do not inherit the generic condition-immunity suppression rule merely because their UI label resembles a condition.

## Reference scope

The implementation in `tools/strain_playtest_rules.py` covers selected namespace lookups, gain/cap/death transitions, point recovery, numeric composition, Dash deadlines and completed-rest accounting. It does not run the campaign, grant class abilities, create inventory, verify all care activities, dispatch conditions or perform resurrection. The caller supplies legality and source eligibility. Its penalty projection does not replace independent life-state, collapse, condition or travel rules.

The namespace lookup rejects unknown/ambiguous sources. Low-level transition helpers such as `expedition_gain` accept already-validated source IDs from their caller; they do not independently repeat the registry lookup.

The [validation report](STRAIN_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) records71 transition checks,30 exact source checks and4,949 maximum-HP invariant states. Broader rest rewards, travel, all-source class semantics, future Strain references, resurrection and human balance remain open.

## Active time and expedition scheduling

**Source recovered from public V5 P11–12 and P88:** an Opening is 100 days, or 2,400 elapsed hours. The V4 system's 240-hour references are stale. Crafting hours represent active work, not free downtime. The recipe records consistently convert a workday to 8 active hours, a workweek to 40, and a workmonth to 160. These are work units, not a promise that every calendar week/month has that many days.

**Completion:** use `activeWorkHours` when present. Five Director-only one-year recipes have null hours; for this framework only, one workyear is 12 workmonths = 1,920 active hours. Preserve their source null and mark the overlay as new; these formulas remain individually unreviewed. A time-mode name is a station/access requirement, not permission to reduce required hours. An eight-hour recipe labeled expedition still needs all eight hours.

Field work requires its actual portable tools and a suitable place. A recipe is field-capable only when its `fieldCraftable` flag permits it; the fact that its trade is generally field-capable is insufficient. Expedition-mode work needs a fortified camp or research station. Workshop work needs a proper workshop. Haven-mode work needs a named secure workshop and storage. Legacy/special work needs a protected long-term facility or an explicitly supported between-season arrangement. Shorter time from a feature does not erase the recipe's station/access requirement.

Schedule one eight-hour Watch at a time. A member assigned to crafting, gathering or preservation can perform compatible sequential tasks within that Watch, recording actual minutes. The unused minutes are not another full team activity. Travel, guarding, assisting, spellcasting, training and work cannot all claim the same minutes; only an explicit ability can authorize concurrent tasks. Each character may schedule at most two active Watches and must satisfy the separately reviewed rest rules; this is a ceiling, not an exemption from fatigue, interruption or danger. For this supplement, an active work Watch means time committed to crafting, harvesting, preservation, trade training, formula research or assisting those activities. The two-Watch ceiling limits this framework's work contribution; it does not by itself resolve whether another reviewed subsystem permits a distinct noncrafting activity in the remaining Watch. Rest, Strain, fatigue and expedition legality continue to come from their own governing rules. An eight-hour beneficial Long Rest cannot simultaneously be eight hours of crafting. Trance's sleep reduction does not shorten the required Long Rest or grant free working time.

Workday notation is normalized to active hours before a valid speed feature applies. Forge Dwarf Master Craftsman reduces eligible artisan-tool creation hours by 25%; use hours × 0.75, rounding upward only to the next whole minute. It does not shorten rest, travel, ingredient growth/spoilage, training, another person's work, harvesting, or a separately fixed natural-remedy/tinker racial procedure. It does not shorten a recipe's independently stated incubation or calendar wait. Other applicable time modifiers require their own actual text; no unprinted stacking multiplier is created here.

Long orders may be paused between active phases. A default phase is at most eight active hours. Completing a phase safely permits secure storage and later resumption without lost progress. Forced interruption inside a phase loses only unfinished progress in that phase; completed phases remain. No crafting roll occurs yet. Reserved perishables still age, and explicit physical destruction can lose actual inventory. There is no arbitrary full restart or repeated free quality roll. Before an uninterrupted-phase order begins, record its phase lengths and storage needs; absent a more specific formula, use this default.

At the season boundary, unfinished work continues only if its actual location, workers and storage remain legally and physically available under the existing campaign rules. The 2,400-hour Opening does not grant 2,400 labor hours per character. The Haven activity 'Brew a Batch' supplies a workday assignment (8 hours), not automatic completion of every recipe regardless of its own duration.

## Material identity, consumption and substitution

Keep the exact recipe ID and component occurrence. Global material names alone are insufficient: 143 embedded names have different tier/price/weight variants. Record identity as the recipe component's name, tier, category, properties, unit weight, unit value and source occurrence. Quantity belongs to the inventory lot, not the identity. Preserve component IDs where supplied; none are silently merged or normalized to a cheaper same-name material. The 2-gp crafting Crystal Vial and 5-gp equipment Vial remain distinct records unless an explicit compatibility/substitution ruling is recorded.

An exact recipe component's stored numeric `tier` remains part of that component's identity and may be compared for that recipe's explicit substitution requirements even when the stored number exceeds 6. This does not extend the generic V4 material-tier ladder or generic harvesting entitlement beyond Tier VI. A Tier 7–10 stored component therefore receives no generic harvest DC, public availability, rarity right or substitution source merely from that number; it requires its actual recipe/source acquisition procedure or another separately reviewed rule.

**Source:** substitutions require the relevant properties and tier unless the recipe names an irreplaceable ingredient. **Completion:** before spending materials, a substitute must satisfy each replaced unit's tier (equal or higher), all required functional properties and role, compatible physical form, and at least its required amount. The Director records the mapping and its actual unit quantities/weights/value. Higher price alone is not compatibility; a higher-tier component does not increase the result tier, quantity or effect. A unique named core cannot be replaced under this general permission. Do not repeatedly change the substitution after observing the outcome.

Reserve consumed quantities at the start and deduct them once at resolution or deliberate abandonment. Abandonment after work starts loses consumed inputs with no product/recovery roll; actual nonconsumed tools and intact independently stored unused supplies remain. Ingredients left outside the reservation remain usable but cannot also fund another order. Return only the exact quantities authorized by Masterwork or ordinary failure, never both for one result. No recovery from a Mishap. Component `consumed=false` returns its full reserved quantity; role=tool is not itself a consumed flag.

Nineteen source component rows have role=tool and consumed=true. Treat these as incorporated parts in those exact recipes, not the separately required reusable toolkit; retain their flags until individual recipe review. A focusing lens incorporated into a device is not a reusable station lens. The work order must supply both if it needs both. Never 'repair' all role=tool rows to nonconsumed in bulk.

Ordinary failure recovery uses each identity's physical units: an indivisible organ, lens, bottle or crystal rounds down to whole units; explicitly divisible bulk reagent can be recorded to 0.01 source units. Recovery never creates money. For example, four ordinary indivisible non-catalyst vials return one; one irreplaceable catalyst returns zero. These recovered lots retain their age and identity. A failed batch cannot be salvaged again for another automatic 25%.

## Armor and shields

Choose one applicable AC formula. Light armor adds the full DEX modifier to its printed base. Medium adds `min(DEX modifier, 2)`, including a negative modifier. Heavy uses its fixed AC without positive or negative DEX. Explicit separate AC bonuses apply only when their own requirements are met.

One usable equipped shield contributes its printed bonus: buckler +1, shield +2, tower shield +3. No second shield bonus. Elven weave's printed Stealth advantage uses ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation. Dwarven plate is AC 18; its descriptive superior protection adds nothing. Scale mail's description adds no slashing resistance. Tower shield adds no unprinted cover or additional movement penalty.

**Nonproficient worn armor.** Retain V6 disadvantage on STR/DEX ability checks, saving throws and attacks. Core replaces the older casting prohibition: spells remain permitted, but an RP-priced spell costs +1 RP once per cast and concentration checks/saves have disadvantage. Multiple nonproficient armor pieces never multiply this surcharge. A normal 0-RP spell using the RP price interface can cost 1 RP. Apply this ordinary price addition before the already reviewed eligible reductions and final Resonance Influence step.

**Nonproficient shield — new completion.** While using a shield without shield proficiency, apply the STR/DEX check/save/attack disadvantage. A shield alone adds neither Core's armor RP surcharge nor concentration disadvantage and does not prohibit casting. Core names worn armor for those casting penalties.

A charge-only ancestry spell, Oracle effect or other cast with no RP-price interface acquires no RP price or pool from nonproficient armor. Actual concentration still has disadvantage from nonproficient worn armor. Hands, spell components and other independent casting restrictions remain.

**Strength minimum — new completion.** If one or more equipped armor/shield records have a listed STR minimum you do not meet, reduce Speed by 10 feet total, minimum 0. This is not a minimum to equip; multiple deficient pieces do not stack the reduction. This penalty can coexist with Load/Burden.

The Dwarf's printed rule that Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor prevents this penalty when the deficient item is heavy armor. It does not waive Load/Burden, another movement penalty or a tower shield's separate STR minimum. If a table chooses V6's preserved optional encumbrance alternate, that alternate ignores the Armor Table Strength column; the active reviewed Load procedure is not that alternate.

| Equipment | Don | Doff |
|---|---|---|
| Light armor | 1 minute | 1 minute |
| Medium armor | 5 minutes | 1 minute |
| Heavy armor | 10 minutes | 5 minutes |
| Any shield | 1 Action | 1 Action |

## Object damage and Sunder

These are **new mundane object procedures** completing the Core Sunder interface. A target must be one actual separately tracked object or explicitly modeled separable component. Naming an armor strap, pin, lace, hinge or seam does not create a cheaper independent target. Construct joints remain subject to the creature's actual stat block.

Sunder uses an actual legal weapon attack against one perceived reachable object/component, consuming one attack when taking the Attack Action. It grants no extra attack or free damage to a wearer. The attacker cannot target a hidden component through a creature or solid obstruction. Against worn/held gear, target AC is the higher of the material AC and wearer's current AC. Unattended gear uses material AC. Ordinary attack eligibility and printed object-target exclusions still apply.

Worn/carried inventory is never damaged merely because its creature is hit. An attack, spell or hazard damages equipment only if its actual rule expressly targets/includes objects, structures, carried gear or that item. Sunder never also damages the wearer unless another source expressly says so.

Objects outside a listed or genuinely comparable category need an actual assigned profile before targeted durability resolution; no automatic structure or artifact certification is implied.

Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage unless an exact rule says otherwise. Establish physical damage compatibility before rolling: a sword cannot chop a liquid. Do not invent retroactive resistances. Use ordinary attack damage and applicable weapon properties; creature-only conditions and resource triggers do not become object-eligible.

At zero structural HP, the object is **Broken** and loses usable AC, weapon, focus, tool or other functional benefits. It still exists, occupies its hand/slot/container and retains mass until dropped, removed or repaired. Broken armor does not disappear. No negative HP, duplicated loot, automatic explosion, passive regeneration or repair from ordinary rest. Magic items/artifacts need their own durability; no mundane default is assigned to unresolved magical gear. True Polymorph's independently excluded-object rules still apply even when an object has HP.

A Broken item grants none of its positive usable benefits, but remains physically worn, held or strapped until removed. It continues to occupy its hand/slot and contribute weight/Load, and retains physical drawbacks from still wearing or carrying it: applicable don/doff requirements, armor Stealth disadvantage, STR-minimum movement penalty and nonproficiency consequences.
